blocks.prompt: 1 (i) Expand the following upto 4 terms, taking the values of \(x\) such that the expansion in each case is valid: \((1 + x)^{-1/3}\)
blocks.explanation:
Yahan power \(-\tfrac{1}{3}\) hai, yani negative bhi aur fraction bhi. Aisi power par binomial expansion kabhi khatam nahi hoti, yeh infinite series (la-mehdood silsila) ban jati hai.
Find kya karna hai? Pehle chaar terms, aur yeh ke \(x\) ki kin values par yeh expansion sahi (valid) hai.
Rule kaunsa? \((1 + x)^{n}\) ki general binomial series, jo sirf \(|x| < 1\) par chalti hai.
Plan: \(n = -\tfrac{1}{3}\) rakhenge, har coefficient ko aaram se simplify karenge, aur aakhir mein condition likhenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \((1 + x)^{-1/3}\).
Humein find karna hai: pehli 4 terms aur \(x\) ki woh values jin par expansion valid hai.
Tareeqa: Jab index (power) negative ya fraction ho to yeh series lagti hai:
\[(1 + x)^{n} = 1 + nx\]
\[+ \dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2!}x^{2}\]
\[+ \dfrac{n(n - 1)(n - 2)}{3!}x^{3} + \dots\]
Yeh series sirf tab sahi jawab deti hai jab \(|x| < 1\) ho. Hamari bracket pehle hi \(1 + x\) ki shakal mein hai, is liye seedha \(n = -\tfrac{1}{3}\) rakh dete hain; kuch bahar nikalne ki zaroorat nahi.

Doosri term
\[nx = -\dfrac{1}{3}x\]
Kyun: Series ki doosri term hamesha \(nx\) hoti hai. Bas \(n\) ki value rakh di. Sign ka khayal rakhein: \(n\) negative hai is liye yeh term minus wali hai.

Teesri term
\[\dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2!} = \dfrac{(-\frac{1}{3})(-\frac{4}{3})}{2}\]
\[= \dfrac{4/9}{2} = \dfrac{2}{9}\]
Kyun: Pehle \(n - 1\) nikalein: \(-\tfrac{1}{3} - 1 = -\tfrac{1}{3} - \tfrac{3}{3} = -\tfrac{4}{3}\). Do negative numbers ka product positive hota hai, is liye \(\tfrac{4}{9}\) aaya. Phir \(2! = 2\) se divide kiya to \(\tfrac{2}{9}\).
Dhyan dein: \(n - 1\) ko \(-\tfrac{2}{3}\) likhna (yani 1 jama kar dena) bahut aam ghalti hai. Negative number mein se 1 minus karne se woh aur zyada negative hota hai.

Chauthi term
\[\dfrac{n(n - 1)(n - 2)}{3!}\]
\[= \dfrac{(-\frac{1}{3})(-\frac{4}{3})(-\frac{7}{3})}{6}\]
\[= \dfrac{-28/27}{6} = -\dfrac{14}{81}\]
Kyun: \(n - 2 = -\tfrac{1}{3} - 2 = -\tfrac{7}{3}\). Ab teen negative factors hain; teen minus ka product minus hota hai. Upar \(1 \times 4 \times 7 = 28\), neeche \(3 \times 3 \times 3 = 27\). Phir \(3! = 6\) se divide: \(\tfrac{28}{162}\), aur 2 se chhota karne par \(\tfrac{14}{81}\).

Expansion likhein
\[(1 + x)^{-1/3} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{3}x\]
\[+ \dfrac{2}{9}x^{2} - \dfrac{14}{81}x^{3} + \dots\]
Kyun: Har coefficient ke saath us ki apni power wala \(x\) lagaya: doosri term ke saath \(x\), teesri ke saath \(x^{2}\), chauthi ke saath \(x^{3}\). Signs ek ke baad ek badal rahe hain (minus, plus, minus), jo negative \(n\) mein aam baat hai.

Valid hone ki condition
\[|x| < 1\]
Kyun: Fraction ya negative power wali series tabhi kisi number ki taraf jaati hai (converge karti hai) jab bracket ki doosri term numerically 1 se chhoti ho. Agar \(x\) bara ho to terms barhti jayengi aur jama ka koi matlab nahi rahega.

Tasdeeq: ek chhoti value rakh kar
\[x = 0.1:\ (1.1)^{-1/3} = 0.968729\dots\]
\[1 - 0.033333 + 0.002222\]
\[- 0.000173 = 0.968716\]
Kyun: Calculator wali asal value aur hamari chaar terms ka jama chaar decimal tak barabar hain. Is ka matlab coefficients sahi hain; agar koi sign ya number ghalat hota to farq foran nazar aa jata.

blocks.prompt: 1 (ii) Expand the following upto 4 terms, taking the values of \(x\) such that the expansion in each case is valid: \((4 - 3x)^{1/2}\)
blocks.explanation:
Is dafa bracket 4 se shuru ho rahi hai, 1 se nahi. Binomial series sirf \((1 + y)^{n}\) ke liye hai, is liye pehle bracket ko "1 + kuch" ki shakal mein lana zaroori hai.
Find kya karna hai? Pehli chaar terms aur \(x\) par condition.
Rule kaunsa? 4 ko bahar nikal kar \(n = \tfrac{1}{2}\) wali series.
Plan: \(4 - 3x = 4(1 - \tfrac{3x}{4})\), phir \(y = -\tfrac{3x}{4}\) rakh kar expand, aur aakhir mein \(\sqrt{4} = 2\) se multiply.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \((4 - 3x)^{1/2}\).
Humein find karna hai: pehli 4 terms aur valid hone ki condition.
Tareeqa: Series \((1 + y)^{n}\) ke liye bani hai. Is liye pehle 4 ko common nikal kar bracket ko 1 se shuru karenge, phir \(n = \tfrac{1}{2}\) wali series lagayenge. Yeh qadam chhorna sab se bari ghalti hogi, kyunke \((4 + \dots)\) par seedhi series lagane se ghalat jawab aata hai.

4 bahar nikalein
\[(4 - 3x)^{1/2} = 4^{1/2}\left(1 - \dfrac{3x}{4}\right)^{1/2}\]
\[= 2(1 + y)^{1/2},\ y = -\dfrac{3x}{4}\]
Kyun: Andar se 4 common liya to \(3x\) ban gaya \(\tfrac{3x}{4}\). Power ka qanoon \((ab)^{n} = a^{n}b^{n}\) kehta hai ke 4 par bhi power \(\tfrac{1}{2}\) lagegi, aur \(4^{1/2} = \sqrt{4} = 2\).
Dhyan dein: 4 bahar aate waqt \(4^{1/2}\) banta hai, sirf 4 nahi. Bahut se students yahan 4 likh dete hain.

\(n = \tfrac{1}{2}\) ke coefficients
\[n = \dfrac{1}{2}\]
\[\dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2!} = \dfrac{\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{1}{2})}{2} = -\dfrac{1}{8}\]
\[\dfrac{n(n - 1)(n - 2)}{3!} = \dfrac{\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{1}{2})(-\frac{3}{2})}{6} = \dfrac{1}{16}\]
Kyun: \(n - 1 = \tfrac{1}{2} - 1 = -\tfrac{1}{2}\) aur \(n - 2 = -\tfrac{3}{2}\). Teesri coefficient mein ek minus hai, is liye negative. Chauthi mein do minus hain, is liye positive: \(\tfrac{3}{8} \div 6 = \tfrac{1}{16}\). Yeh \(n = \tfrac{1}{2}\) wale coefficients yaad rakhne layak hain, square root ke har sawal mein kaam aate hain.

\(y\) mein expansion
\[(1 + y)^{1/2} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}y\]
\[- \dfrac{1}{8}y^{2} + \dfrac{1}{16}y^{3} + \dots\]
Kyun: Upar wale coefficients general series mein rakh diye. Abhi \(y\) hi rehne diya taa ke kaam saaf rahe; \(x\) baad mein daalenge.

\(y = -\tfrac{3x}{4}\) rakhein
\[\dfrac{1}{2}y = -\dfrac{3}{8}x\]
\[-\dfrac{1}{8}y^{2} = -\dfrac{1}{8} \cdot \dfrac{9x^{2}}{16} = -\dfrac{9}{128}x^{2}\]
\[\dfrac{1}{16}y^{3} = \dfrac{1}{16} \cdot \dfrac{-27x^{3}}{64}\]
\[= -\dfrac{27}{1024}x^{3}\]
Kyun: \(y\) negative hai. Negative ka square positive hota hai, is liye \(y^{2} = \tfrac{9x^{2}}{16}\); lekin negative ka cube negative rehta hai, is liye \(y^{3} = -\tfrac{27x^{3}}{64}\). Is wajah se chauthi term bhi minus ban gayi, halaanke coefficient \(\tfrac{1}{16}\) positive tha.

2 se multiply karein
\[(4 - 3x)^{1/2} = 2 - \dfrac{3}{4}x\]
\[- \dfrac{9}{64}x^{2} - \dfrac{27}{512}x^{3} + \dots\]
Kyun: Bracket ke bahar wala 2 har term ko double karta hai: \(2 \cdot \tfrac{3}{8} = \tfrac{3}{4}\), \(2 \cdot \tfrac{9}{128} = \tfrac{9}{64}\), \(2 \cdot \tfrac{27}{1024} = \tfrac{27}{512}\).

Valid hone ki condition
\[\left|-\dfrac{3x}{4}\right| < 1\]
\[|x| < \dfrac{4}{3}\]
Kyun: Series \(y\) mein bani hai, is liye condition \(|y| < 1\) hai. Modulus mein minus ka koi asar nahi, phir dono taraf \(\tfrac{4}{3}\) se multiply kiya. Yani yahan \(x\) ki range 1 se thori bari hai, kyunke \(x\) ke saath \(\tfrac{3}{4}\) laga hua hai.

Tasdeeq: ek chhoti value rakh kar
\[x = 0.1:\ \sqrt{3.7} = 1.923538\dots\]
\[2 - 0.075 - 0.001406\]
\[- 0.000053 = 1.923541\]
Kyun: Chaar terms ka jama asal value se paanch decimal tak mil gaya, to expansion sahi hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key mein doosri term \(-\frac{2}{4}x\) chhapi hai, jo ghalat hai. Sahi coefficient \(2 \times \frac{3}{8} = \frac{3}{4}\) hai, yani jawab \(2 - \frac{3}{4}x - \frac{9}{64}x^{2} - \frac{27}{512}x^{3} + \dots\), \(|x| < \frac{4}{3}\). Baqi terms key mein sahi hain. Khud \(x = 0.1\) rakh kar check kar lijiye.

blocks.prompt: 1 (iii) Expand the following upto 4 terms, taking the values of \(x\) such that the expansion in each case is valid: \(\frac{(1 - x)^{-1}}{(1 + x)^{2}}\)
blocks.explanation:
Yahan ek nahi, do brackets hain: \((1 - x)^{-1}\) upar aur \((1 + x)^{2}\) neeche. Dono ki apni apni binomial series banegi.
Find kya karna hai? Poore expression ki pehli chaar terms aur valid hone ki condition.
Rule kaunsa? Neeche wali bracket ko negative power de kar upar laana, dono ki series, phir do series ka product.
Plan: dono ko \(x^{3}\) tak expand karna, multiply kar ke har power ke coefficients ehtiyat se jama karna.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\frac{(1 - x)^{-1}}{(1 + x)^{2}}\).
Humein find karna hai: pehli 4 terms aur condition.
Tareeqa: Denominator ko negative power ke saath upar le aayenge, taa ke poora expression do brackets ka product ban jaye. Phir dono brackets ko binomial series se khol kar multiply karenge. Sirf \(x^{3}\) tak ki terms chahiye, is liye us se bari powers chhor denge.

Product ki shakal mein likhein
\[\dfrac{(1 - x)^{-1}}{(1 + x)^{2}} = (1 - x)^{-1}(1 + x)^{-2}\]
Kyun: Qanoon \(\tfrac{1}{a^{m}} = a^{-m}\): jo cheez neeche power \(2\) ke saath thi, woh upar power \(-2\) ke saath aa gayi. Ab division nahi, sirf multiplication bacha, jo asaan hai.

\((1 - x)^{-1}\) kholein
\[(1 - x)^{-1} = 1 + x + x^{2} + x^{3} + \dots\]
Kyun: Yahan \(n = -1\) aur formula wale \(x\) ki jagah \(-x\) hai. Coefficients \(-1, 1, -1\) aate hain aur yeh \((-x), (-x)^{2}, (-x)^{3}\) se multiply hote hain. Minus mein minus plus, is liye saari terms positive ho gayin. Yeh series itni aam hai ke zabani yaad kar lijiye.

\((1 + x)^{-2}\) kholein
\[(1 + x)^{-2} = 1 - 2x + 3x^{2} - 4x^{3} + \dots\]
Kyun: \(n = -2\): doosri term \(nx = -2x\); teesri \(\tfrac{(-2)(-3)}{2} = 3\); chauthi \(\tfrac{(-2)(-3)(-4)}{6} = -4\). Coefficients 1, 2, 3, 4 hain aur signs badalte jate hain. Yeh pattern bhi yaad rakhne wala hai.

Multiply kar ke har power jama karein
\[\text{const}: 1\]
\[x: -2 + 1 = -1\]
\[x^{2}: 3 - 2 + 1 = 2\]
\[x^{3}: -4 + 3 - 2 + 1 = -2\]
Kyun: \(x^{k}\) ka coefficient nikalne ke liye pehli series ki \(x^{a}\) aur doosri ki \(x^{b}\) wali terms ke woh saare jore lete hain jin mein \(a + b = k\). Masalan \(x^{2}\): \(1 \cdot 3x^{2}\), \(x \cdot (-2x)\) aur \(x^{2} \cdot 1\), yani \(3 - 2 + 1\).
Dhyan dein: koi jora chhoot na jaye. \(x^{3}\) ke liye chaar jore hain; ek bhi bhool gaye to jawab ghalat.

Expansion likhein
\[= 1 - x + 2x^{2} - 2x^{3} + \dots\]
Kyun: Jama kiye hue coefficients ko unki powers ke saath likh diya.

Valid hone ki condition
\[|x| < 1\]
Kyun: Pehli series ko \(|-x| < 1\) chahiye aur doosri ko \(|x| < 1\); dono ek hi baat hain. Product tabhi sahi hai jab dono series sahi hon, is liye \(|x| < 1\).

Tasdeeq: ek chhoti value rakh kar
\[x = 0.1:\ \dfrac{1}{0.9 \times 1.21} = 0.918274\dots\]
\[1 - 0.1 + 0.02 - 0.002 = 0.918\]
Kyun: Teen decimal tak barabar. Jo chhota sa farq hai woh agli term \(3x^{4} \approx 0.0003\) ki wajah se hai, jo humne chhor di thi.

blocks.prompt: 1 (iv) Expand the following upto 4 terms, taking the values of \(x\) such that the expansion in each case is valid: \(\frac{\sqrt{1 + 2x}}{1 - x}\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh bhi do series ka product hai: upar square root \((1 + 2x)^{1/2}\) aur neeche \((1 - x)\), jo upar aa kar \((1 - x)^{-1}\) ban jayega.
Find kya karna hai? Pehli chaar terms, aur \(x\) ki woh values jahan DONO series ek saath sahi hon.
Rule kaunsa? Har bracket ki binomial series, phir multiply.
Plan: dono ko \(x^{3}\) tak kholna, powers jama karna, aur do conditions mein se sakht (chhoti) wali chunna.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\frac{\sqrt{1 + 2x}}{1 - x}\).
Humein find karna hai: pehli 4 terms aur condition.
Tareeqa: Square root ko power \(\tfrac{1}{2}\) aur denominator ko power \(-1\) bana kar \((1 + 2x)^{1/2}(1 - x)^{-1}\) likhenge, phir dono ko kholenge aur multiply karenge.

\((1 + 2x)^{1/2}\) kholein
\[= 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}(2x) - \dfrac{1}{8}(2x)^{2} + \dfrac{1}{16}(2x)^{3}\]
\[= 1 + x - \dfrac{1}{2}x^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}x^{3} + \dots\]
Kyun: \(n = \tfrac{1}{2}\) ke coefficients \(\tfrac{1}{2}, -\tfrac{1}{8}, \tfrac{1}{16}\) part (ii) mein nikal chuke hain. Yahan formula ke \(x\) ki jagah \(2x\) hai, is liye poora \(2x\) power mein jata hai: \((2x)^{2} = 4x^{2}\), \((2x)^{3} = 8x^{3}\). Phir \(-\tfrac{1}{8} \cdot 4 = -\tfrac{1}{2}\) aur \(\tfrac{1}{16} \cdot 8 = \tfrac{1}{2}\).
Dhyan dein: \((2x)^{2}\) ko \(2x^{2}\) likhna aam ghalti hai; 2 ka bhi square hota hai.

\((1 - x)^{-1}\) kholein
\[(1 - x)^{-1} = 1 + x + x^{2} + x^{3} + \dots\]
Kyun: Yeh wohi series hai jo part (iii) mein bani thi: saari terms plus aur sab coefficients 1.

Multiply kar ke har power jama karein
\[x: 1 + 1 = 2\]
\[x^{2}: 1 + 1 - \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}\]
\[x^{3}: 1 + 1 - \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} = 2\]
Kyun: Doosri series ke saare coefficients 1 hain, is liye ek mazedaar shortcut milta hai: \(x^{k}\) ka coefficient pehli series ke shuru se \(x^{k}\) tak ke coefficients ka jama hai. Masalan \(x^{2}\): \(1 + 1 - \tfrac{1}{2} = \tfrac{3}{2}\).

Expansion likhein
\[\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + 2x}}{1 - x} = 1 + 2x + \dfrac{3}{2}x^{2}\]
\[+ 2x^{3} + \dots\]
Kyun: Jama kiye hue coefficients likh diye.

Valid hone ki condition
\[|2x| < 1 \Rightarrow |x| < \dfrac{1}{2}\]
\[|x| < 1\]
\[\text{both: } |x| < \dfrac{1}{2}\]
Kyun: Pehli series ko \(|2x| < 1\) yani \(|x| < \tfrac{1}{2}\) chahiye, doosri ko \(|x| < 1\). Dono ek saath tab sahi hongi jab \(|x| < \tfrac{1}{2}\) ho, kyunke jo \(x\) \(\tfrac{1}{2}\) se chhota hai woh 1 se bhi chhota hai. Hamesha sakht condition chuni jati hai.
Dhyan dein: sirf \(|x| < 1\) likh dena ghalat hai; masalan \(x = 0.8\) par \(\sqrt{1 + 2x}\) wali series kaam nahi karti.

Tasdeeq: ek chhoti value rakh kar
\[x = 0.1:\ \dfrac{\sqrt{1.2}}{0.9} = 1.217161\dots\]
\[1 + 0.2 + 0.015 + 0.002 = 1.217\]
Kyun: Teen decimal tak barabar, to coefficients sahi hain.
